testPolicy.text: The UW System Board of Regents authorized UW-Madison to waive the ACT/SAT requirement for first-year applicants through the spring 2028 term: students applying for spring 2027, fall 2027 and spring 2028 do not have to submit a score and are not disadvantaged without one. No decision yet for fall 2028 and beyond; the university recommends planning to take a test.
testPolicy.since: test-optional since the 2020 waiver; current waiver runs through the spring 2028 term

cost.totalIncludes: Office of Student Financial Aid, 2026-27 estimated academic-year cost of attendance (nine months, full time): tuition and fees, required course materials and supplies, housing and meals, personal, transportation, loan fees 68. Not included: a new student fee of about 330 for first-year students, the 1,100 computer allowance added for incoming undergraduates, and tuition differentials (engineering about 3,200, nursing 1,500, business 3,000).

inState.note: tuition line is 'Tuition & Fees'; CDS 2025-26 G1: tuition 10,716.72 plus required fees 1,699.48

outOfState.note: Minnesota residents (tuition reciprocity) have their own column: tuition and fees 18,328, transportation 866, total 37,574

aidPromise.text: Bucky's Tuition Promise guarantees scholarships and grants that pay tuition and segregated fees for Wisconsin resident students whose household adjusted gross income is $65,000 or less: eight consecutive semesters (4 years) for incoming first-year students, four semesters for transfers. Only income, not assets, counts. Bucky's Pell Pathway adds, for Pell Grant-eligible Wisconsin residents, grants, scholarships and work-study sufficient to meet financial need without loans.

deadlines.early: November 1 (Early Action, non-binding, materials by November 9, decision on or before January 31)
deadlines.regular: January 15 (Regular Decision, materials by January 22, decision on or before March 31)

facts.text: For fall 2025, UW-Madison admitted 5,672 of 10,058 Wisconsin applicants and 19,948 of 49,463 out-of-state applicants; 3,831 of the 8,495 enrolled first-years were Wisconsin residents.
Bucky's Tuition Promise covers four years of tuition and segregated fees for Wisconsin residents whose household adjusted gross income is $65,000 or less, counting income only, not assets.
Minnesota residents pay a reciprocity rate: their 2026-27 budget is 37,574, against 31,524 for Wisconsin residents and 65,120 for other nonresidents.
Testing is optional for applicants through the spring 2028 term, and only 1,000 of the fall 2025 enrolled first-years submitted an SAT score, against 2,437 who sent an ACT.
Engineering, nursing and business students pay a tuition differential on top of the standard budget (estimated 3,200, 1,500 and 3,000 a year).
For fall 2025, 4,317 students accepted a place on the waiting list and 1,088 of them were admitted.

notes: CDS 2025-26 Excel downloaded from UW-Madison's Box link listed on data.wisc.edu (file id 2339108500297). C1: applied 36,086 men + 37,800 women + 26 unknown = 73,912; admitted 13,597 + 16,559 + 11 = 30,167; enrolled 3,524 + 4,971 = 8,495. C9: 11.8% submitted the SAT, 28.7% the ACT. C12 GPA 3.91 (94% submitting). CDS G1 2026-27: tuition 10,716.72 in-state, 44,232 out-of-state (45,232.08 nonresident alien), required fees 1,699.48, food and housing 14,994; 25.3% of undergraduates pay more than G1 because of program differentials. The 2025-26 budget on the same page was 30,644 resident and 63,268 nonresident.
